patient_selection.evidence: This dataset includes 3D T1 MP-RAGE, 3D T2 FLAIR, 2D T1 STIR, and 2D T2 TSE acquisitions with instructed head nodding and shaking motion from 22 healthy participants.
patient_selection.rationale: Healthy volunteer convenience samples from two research datasets with deliberately induced motion; no consecutive or random clinical sampling frame is described.

index_test.evidence: The metrics were recalculated seven times with varying pre-processing steps.
index_test.rationale: The index metrics were computed automatically but no threshold was pre-specified and seven pre-processing variants were explored, with the best-correlating configuration reported post hoc.

reference_standard.evidence: the limited quality evaluation (only one experienced radiologist for the CUBRIC dataset versus two radiologists and two technicians for the NRU dataset)
reference_standard.rationale: The reference is a subjective 1-5 quality score with only moderate observer agreement for three of four sequences and a single rater in one dataset.

flow_timing.evidence: Each sequence was acquired with and without voluntary motion, as well as with and without prospective motion correction. The acquisition without motion and without motion correction served as reference image.
flow_timing.rationale: Index and reference images come from the same within-session paired acquisitions, so the interval is negligible and all rated volumes entered the correlation analysis.

app_patient_selection.evidence: Our current analysis is based on data acquired for research purposes that included a separate 'still' reference scan.
app_patient_selection.rationale: Healthy research volunteers performing instructed motion do not represent a clinical brain MRI population undergoing accelerated reconstruction.

app_index_test.evidence: the use of IQMs for benchmarking different image reconstruction or motion correction methods is challenging and might misguide future research
app_index_test.rationale: The index test is a panel of image quality metrics for motion correction rather than an accelerated or AI reconstruction, so it addresses the review question only indirectly.

app_reference_standard.evidence: radiological evaluation of overall image quality is commonly used as a gold standard when investigating the performance of IQMs
app_reference_standard.rationale: Expert radiologist reading plus a motion-free reference acquisition matches the review's definition of the reference standard.

patient_selection.evidence: 100 consecutive patients with various neurological conditions underwent both T2(DR) and T2(CN) on a Siemens Vida 3 T scanner
patient_selection.rationale: Consecutive enrolment of an unselected clinical neurological cohort, with no case-control construction or stated inappropriate exclusions.

index_test.evidence: Four neuroradiologists evaluated overall image quality (OIQ), diagnostic safety (DS), and image artifacts (IA), blinded to the acquisition mode.
index_test.rationale: Readers scoring the deep-learning reconstruction were explicitly blinded to whether the acquisition was accelerated or conventional.

reference_standard.evidence: To compare clinical ratings and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) measures of a commercially available Deep Learning-based MRI reconstruction method (T2(DR)) against conventional T2- turbo spin echo brain MRI (T2(CN)).
reference_standard.rationale: The comparator is the full-length conventional T2 turbo spin echo acquisition, rated by the same readers under blinding to acquisition mode.

flow_timing.evidence: underwent both T2(DR) and T2(CN) on a Siemens Vida 3 T scanner with a 64-channel head coil in the same examination
flow_timing.rationale: Both sequences were acquired in the same examination so the interval is effectively zero, and results are reported for the full cohort of 100 patients.

app_patient_selection.evidence: The mean patient age was 43.6 years (SD 20.3), with 54 females.
app_patient_selection.rationale: A routine clinical adult neurological population undergoing brain MRI matches the review question.

app_index_test.evidence: Acquisition times were 3.33 min for T2(CN) and 1.04 min for T2(DR).
app_index_test.rationale: A commercial deep-learning reconstruction delivering a roughly three-fold reduction in acquisition time is exactly the index test of interest.

app_reference_standard.evidence: Our results suggest that while T2(DR) may be clinically applicable for a diagnostic setting, it does not fully match the quality of high-standard conventional T2(CN), MRI acquisitions.
app_reference_standard.rationale: The standard-of-care conventional acquisition read by neuroradiologists is the reference standard the review specifies.

patient_selection.evidence: This study was conducted retrospectively using ethically acquired publicly available human subject data.
patient_selection.rationale: Convenience reuse of two public datasets built by design around paired motion-free and deliberately motion-corrupted scans, with no consecutive or random clinical sampling rule.

index_test.evidence: To train the network, we utilize paired datasets where motion-affected images (simulated via our framework) serve as inputs, and their corresponding ground-truth, artifact-free images act as targets. During training, we optimize using the SSIM loss function.
index_test.rationale: The correction network is optimised against the same similarity measure later used to judge it and no blinded reading or pre-specified diagnostic threshold was applied, although test patients were held out.

reference_standard.evidence: For each patient, there are three scans: one motion-free scan acquired while the patient remained still and two motion-affected scans acquired while the patient purposefully moved their head to induce artifacts.
reference_standard.rationale: A genuinely acquired motion-free scan of the same subject serves as ground truth rather than a simulation.

flow_timing.evidence: we applied normalization and performed registration to align the motion-free and motion-affected images in the MR-ART dataset, as the volumes were often misaligned.
flow_timing.rationale: Index and reference images came from separate acquisitions that were frequently misaligned and required registration, and the number of subjects and slices in the final MR-ART test set is not reported.

app_patient_selection.evidence: The motion artifacts in the MR-ART dataset were generated through purposeful movement, which differs from the unintentional and often irregular motion seen in real-world clinical settings.
app_patient_selection.rationale: The population is volunteers performing instructed head movements rather than a clinical cohort whose diagnostic content is at stake.

app_index_test.evidence: DIMA (DIffusing Motion Artifacts), a novel framework that leverages diffusion models to enable unsupervised motion artifact correction in brain MRI.
app_index_test.rationale: A deep-learning generative method that alters brain MRI image content falls within the review's index test of AI-based reconstruction and restoration.

app_reference_standard.evidence: To validate performance, we quantify restoration accuracy using as metrics structural similarity index (SSIM), mean squared error (MSE) and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR).
app_reference_standard.rationale: The reference acquisition is compared only by global similarity metrics, with no radiologist reading or lesion-level assessment of preserved diagnostic content.

patient_selection.evidence: Patient data were consecutively acquired on a 3 T Philips Ingenia Elition scanner equipped with a 32-channel head coil between 08/2021 and 02/2023.
patient_selection.rationale: Consecutive acquisition of routine clinical scans over a defined period, with a documented and diagnosis-independent exclusion of five motion-degraded cases.

index_test.evidence: The order of the reconstruction methods was randomized, and the raters remained unaware of the method used and the patients' clinical information.
index_test.rationale: Reconstruction identity was randomised and concealed from all three raters, who were also blinded to clinical information.

reference_standard.evidence: For the prospectively acquired patient data, no ground truth data were available, and comparisons with clinically used CS reconstructions prohibited an assessment of changes in diagnosis.
reference_standard.rationale: No fully sampled reference exists; the comparator is a compressed-sensing reconstruction of the same 12-fold undersampled data, so the reference cannot establish whether diagnostic content was preserved.

flow_timing.evidence: Five subjects were discarded due to excessive motion artifacts, in which there was no exclusion bias toward a particular diagnostic label, resulting in a dataset of fifty-seven (n = 57) subjects.
flow_timing.rationale: Both reconstructions derive from identical raw k-space so the interval is zero, all remaining subjects received the same comparator, and withdrawals are fully accounted for.

app_patient_selection.evidence: All patients included in this study (n = 62, 34 females) came to the hospital as part of the clinical routine, including patients with stroke (n = 8)
app_patient_selection.rationale: A heterogeneous routine clinical cohort with stroke, multiple sclerosis and tumours matches the review's target population.

app_index_test.evidence: Twelve-fold accelerated 3D T2-FLAIR images were obtained from a cohort of 62 patients with neurological deficits on 3 T MRI.
app_index_test.rationale: A physics-informed deep-learning reconstruction of highly accelerated prospectively undersampled brain data is precisely the index test of interest.

app_reference_standard.evidence: Compressed sensing (CS) is the reference reconstruction method used in the clinic to which we compare our CIRIM method.
app_reference_standard.rationale: The reference is another accelerated reconstruction rather than a fully sampled acquisition, so preserved diagnostic content cannot be verified against a true standard.

patient_selection.evidence: although we consecutively enrolled pediatric patients who underwent brain MRI during a specified period, there may have been a selection bias associated with the retrospective design of this study
patient_selection.rationale: Consecutive enrolment is claimed but the sample was deliberately capped at the minimum number the institution deemed necessary and the authors concede possible selection bias.

index_test.evidence: Readers were also blinded to the MRI acquisition parameters and sequence identifiers.
index_test.rationale: The three qualitative readers scored a randomised mixture of conventional, accelerated and deep-learning reconstructions while blinded to sequence identity.

reference_standard.evidence: For the qualitative analysis of lesion conspicuity, only images with visible lesions on conventional pre- and post-contrast T1-weighted examinations were included.
reference_standard.rationale: Lesion truth is defined by the comparator images themselves and readers were given lesion locations in advance, producing incorporation bias; the conventional protocol is also already accelerated rather than fully sampled.

flow_timing.evidence: For the quantitative analysis of MRI quality obtained using pre-contrast T1-weighted image sequences, three patients were excluded due to severe postoperative tissue defects (n = 1) or hypomyelination disease (n = 2).
flow_timing.rationale: All three image sets were obtained in the same examination so the interval is zero, and every exclusion is enumerated in a flow chart with all 46 patients retained for qualitative analysis.

app_patient_selection.evidence: In total, 46 patients (20 male and 26 female) with a mean age of 7.4 years (age range: 5 months to 16 years) were included.
app_patient_selection.rationale: A clinical paediatric brain MRI population with varied indications is a relevant, if age-specific, target group for accelerated reconstruction.

app_index_test.evidence: images acquired using the accelerated acquisition protocol were reconstructed using intensity Filter A and a DL-based reconstruction algorithm (AIRTM Recon DL; GE HealthCare)
app_index_test.rationale: A commercial deep-learning reconstruction applied to prospectively accelerated 3D T1 acquisitions matches the review's index test.

app_reference_standard.evidence: All images acquired using the conventional acquisition protocol were reconstructed using intensity Filter A (i.e., slight sharpening and smoothing) reconstruction (ClariView; GE HealthCare)
app_reference_standard.rationale: The institution's standard-of-care conventional protocol acquired in the same session, read by radiologists, is the review's intended comparator.

patient_selection.evidence: In the ranking part of this study we included axial T1, T1 post-contrast, T2, and T2FLAIR 2D images (N = 378, 428, 1894, and 216, respectively) from the fastMRI Initiative neuro database.
patient_selection.rationale: Slices were drawn from a public database with no stated patient-level sampling rule, no demographics and no description of how cases were chosen.

index_test.evidence: A total of 2916 corrupted image pairs were shown to radiologists with random repeats and random left/right ordering on a HTML page.
index_test.rationale: The ranking task was randomised with concealed left/right ordering and repeat presentations, and readers were given no cues about the corruption applied.

reference_standard.evidence: Image ranking was subjective with a high level of intraobserver agreement ( 94.9 % ± 2.4 % ) and lower interobserver agreement ( 61.47 % ± 5.51 % )
reference_standard.rationale: Fully sampled k-space provides a sound image reference, but the radiologist consensus ranking used as the human reference standard showed only moderate interobserver agreement.

flow_timing.evidence: considering the difference in their time commitment, the numbers of rankings from readers varied, which may introduce bias in the majority vote.
flow_timing.rationale: Image pairs did not all receive the same reference standard because readers contributed very unequal numbers of rankings and could skip pairs, biasing the consensus label.

app_patient_selection.evidence: The study is retrospective only and the dataset only consisted of axial brain scans.
app_patient_selection.rationale: The scans are real clinical brain MRI but no clinical indications, pathology prevalence or patient characteristics are reported, so population match cannot be judged.

app_index_test.evidence: We undersampled the multichannel k-space data by Poisson disc with an acceleration factor of 16X.
app_index_test.rationale: Model-based deep-learning reconstruction of 8-fold and 16-fold undersampled brain k-space is directly within the review's index test.

app_reference_standard.evidence: Synthetically corrupted image pairs were ranked by radiologists (N = 7), with a subset also scoring images using a Likert scale (N = 2).
app_reference_standard.rationale: Radiologists judged synthetically corrupted images rather than the accelerated reconstructions themselves, which were compared to the fully sampled reference by automated metrics only.
